version.changelog:
- Removed the sample file skill-card.md.
- No functional or interface changes to the skill itself.
- Documentation (SKILL.md) was unchanged, aside from unrelated descriptive or formatting edits.

llm.summary: This browser automation skill is useful but needs Review because it exposes unauthenticated local browser/code execution and uses a vulnerable Playwright dependency range.

dimensions.detail: The skill is intended for a local trusted visible-browser workflow and binds to 127.0.0.1, which is proportionate for local automation, but it can visit arbitrary sites while a persistent unauthenticated localhost command daemon remains available.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The install path relies on npm install with playwright declared as ^1.51.0 and no lockfile; public advisories list playwright versions before 1.55.1 as affected by CVE-2025-59288, fixed in 1.55.1. ([github.com](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-7mvr-c777-76hp))
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The documentation warns users to confirm risky actions, but the implementation provides eval and run-code over the daemon API without an enforced confirmation gate, allowlist, authentication, or origin check.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The daemon intentionally persists browser and page state across commands and writes state under ~/.pw-browser; shutdown is documented, but persistence plus arbitrary browser-code commands creates sensitive session and data-mutation risk without technical containment.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated browser-automation purpose fits opening pages, snapshots, clicks, forms, screenshots, tabs, and visible non-headless operation, but the same skill also exposes eval and run-code as normal capabilities for arbitrary page and Playwright code execution with real site-action authority.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only in a trusted local environment, close the daemon when done, avoid using it on sensitive authenticated sites unless you are actively supervising, do not run code snippets from webpages or untrusted sources, and update/pin Playwright to a fixed non-vulnerable version with a lockfile before relying on it.
llm.findings:
[TP4] expected: The high-power browser automation capabilities are real and mostly disclosed in SKILL.md, so this is not deceptive, but the persistent daemon and arbitrary execution are material Review concerns.
[SDI-2] expected: pw-browser.js implements eval and run-code; these are expected for advanced Playwright automation but are high-impact because they can read page state and trigger real web actions.
[SDI-1] expected: references/running-code.md openly documents run-code and warns against unknown code, which reduces deception concern but does not add enforcement.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The absence of an enforced confirmation, authentication, allowlist, or origin boundary around eval and run-code is not necessary for the stated purpose and is the strongest policy concern.
[SC1] unexpected: The caret dependency range and missing lockfile are not malicious, but they reduce reproducibility for a browser-control skill.
[SC4] unexpected: The declared Playwright range starts at 1.51.0, and public advisory data identifies versions below 1.55.1 as affected, making upgrade guidance material. ([github.com](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-7mvr-c777-76hp))
